description: Synthetic sample RFP generated by `python -m rfp_copilot.cli sample-rfp`. Requirements are known by construction (the RFP text was written for this project). Two requirements (native mobile app, AI chatbot) are deliberately not covered by the knowledge base.

requirements.text: The vendor shall conduct discovery with City staff and residents before design begins.
The vendor shall provide at least two homepage design concepts that reflect the City's brand.
The website must use a mobile-first, responsive design that works on phones, tablets and desktops.
The CMS must allow non-technical staff to update content without HTML knowledge.
The CMS must provide role-based permissions so that each department edits only its own pages, with an optional approval workflow.
Staff must be able to schedule content to publish and to expire at a set date and time.
The CMS should allow editors to edit content directly on the front end of the site.
Hidden or deleted pages must not continue to appear in search engine results.
The website shall include a single community calendar that all departments can post to, with filtering by category.
The website shall include a section to post bids and RFPs with addenda and vendor notifications.
Staff must sign in using single sign-on with the City's Microsoft Entra ID.
The website must provide access to the City's online utility payment portal.
The website should integrate with the City's parks and recreation registration system.
The vendor should provide a native mobile application for iOS and Android.
The website must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA and comply with ADA Title II requirements.
The vendor shall not use accessibility overlay tools or widgets.
The vendor shall migrate existing content and documents and set up redirects from old page addresses to preserve search rankings.
The vendor must host the website with at least 99.9% uptime.
The vendor must provide SSL certificates, daily backups and a disaster recovery plan.
The vendor should offer an AI chatbot that answers resident questions in real time.
The vendor shall provide training for administrators and content editors, with written documentation.
The vendor must respond to critical issues within 2 hours, 24 hours a day.
The vendor should provide a warranty period after launch.
Proposers must provide at least three references from municipal website projects completed in the last five years.
Proposers must carry general liability and cyber liability insurance.
Proposals must be submitted as a single PDF of no more than 25 pages.
The deadline for submission is 20 January 2027 at 2:00 p.m. local time.
Pricing must be submitted separately using the pricing form in Attachment B.
